claim_limits: The public evidence does not establish campaign SSB EPRE, conducted SSB power, cable loss, as-installed EIRP, or exact NEMO RSRP filtering and combining semantics.
The historical 26.5 dBm configuration and nominal 17.9 dBi antenna gain must not be combined as the December 2025 campaign SSB EIRP.
The installed antenna is reported as VV-65A-R2, while the cited current manufacturer page is for VV-65A-R2-V2; its gain is nominal, not an as-installed measurement.
PUSCH/PUCCH path-loss fields are supported by Nemo products but are not present in the published CSV export; collection or retention cannot be inferred.
SS-RSRP and SS-SINR retain UE implementation choices, so empirical distribution agreement must not be labelled physical measurement equivalence.

claims: Poster P-2.15 is titled Validating Remote Driving via Field Characterization and Inter-Slice Connectivity.
The abstract describes the n40 single-user baseline and Nemo/IxChariot campaign context.
The campaign poster reports the field-characterization results associated with the UPV remote-driving campaign.
Pages 374-378 report UPV 5G SA n40 with 20 MHz, ASUS Snapdragon Insiders and Samsung S25 UEs, Nemo Handy and IxChariot, and Test 1 as the single-user survey.
The reported campaign ranges are approximately -95 to -75 dBm RSRP and 8 to 26 dB SINR.
Page 123 identifies the UPV Nokia n40 SA deployment, AZNA n40 radio, and CommScope VV-65A-R2 antenna.
Pages 46-48 describe historical maximum-power configurations of 46 dBm and 26.5 dBm and call 26.5 dBm the then-current n40 configuration.
This is historical configuration evidence, not campaign SSB power or EPRE.
The VV-65A-R2-V2 manufacturer page lists nominal 17.9 dBi gain in the 2300-2500 MHz range.
Pages 3-4 list serving-cell RSRP separately from beam type/index and list PUSCH/PUCCH path-loss capabilities.
The product sheet does not resolve the averaging, filtering, beam-selection, or antenna-combining semantics of this campaign export.
evidence.source_title: Keysight Nemo Handy and Nemo Walker Air data sheet

claims: Page 10 leaves the SS-RSRP resource-element count to the UE and permits specified receiver-diversity processing choices.
Page 14 documents related SS-SINR implementation choices, preventing an unqualified physical-equivalence claim.

permitted_targets: within-unit median-centred relative RSRP distribution shape
prohibited_claims: physical propagation-loss inference from positive ploss
absolute RFsim noise-power calibration from NEMO SINR
joint physical posterior or ABC acceptance
